title: Affine perfect-complex cut after a surjective fibre map
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let p be a prime ideal of R, and let K be a bounded-above complex of finite free R-modules. Assume that the canonical map H^0(K) tensor_R kappa(p) to H^0(K tensor_R^L kappa(p)) [def-pc-module-cohomology-base-change] is surjective. Then there is f not in p such that, in the derived category D(R_f), K tensor_R R_f is isomorphic to tau_{<=0}(K tensor_R R_f) direct-sum tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f), and tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f) is represented by a bounded complex of finite projective R_f-modules in degrees at least 1; in particular tau_{>=1}(K tensor_R R_f) is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] of Tor-amplitude in [1,infinity).

proof.text: Put F = kappa(p) tensor_R -. The assumed epimorphism on H^0 makes the canonical map F(Z^0 K) to Z^0(FK) epic: compare the right-exact rows K^{-1} -> Z^0 K -> H^0 K and FK^{-1} -> Z^0(FK) -> H^0(FK), and apply the three lemma. Compare next F(Z^0 K) -> FK^0 -> F(im d^0) with the exact row Z^0(FK) -> FK^0 -> FK^1. The middle comparison is the identity, the first comparison is epic, and the top last arrow is epic. The four lemma gives that F(im d^0) -> FK^1 is monic. These are the private cycles and image comparison lemmas; they require no freeness.

The image of d^0 is finite as a quotient of finite K^0, while K^1 is finite projective. Apply the finite-source version of [lem-pc-finite-projective-cokernel-localization] to the image inclusion and the injectivity just proved. For some f outside p its cokernel is finite projective. Extension of scalars preserves epimorphisms, so the cokernel of the localized image inclusion is the cokernel of the localized differential, namely the degree-one opcycles. Thus P = truncGE 1 of the localized complex has finite projective degree-one term, the original localized finite free terms above one, and zero terms below one. The original upper bound gives a bound b = max(c,1). P itself is the required representative and proves perfectness. Its projective terms are flat, so torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat gives the requested tensor lower bound.

Use the distinguished triangle obtained from the short exact truncation sequence. Its third object is canonically isomorphic to Q(P). The finite projective terms of P are categorically projective and vanish outside [1,b]. The first object Q(truncLE 0) has zero cohomology in degrees at least two. Apply the splitting clause of [lem-pc-derived-splitting-unique] with a = 1 and transport the right summand along the canonical isomorphism. This proves the stated direct-sum isomorphism.
